title: Build a custom skill

em: Teach the AI a job you already do well.
lead: The best skills are not clever. They are a job you already do well, written down in the order you do it, with the rules you follow without thinking. Here is the template, how to test it, and the three mistakes that make most skills fail.
tiles: The template, the test, and the three mistakes.
Watch you do the job once, then write the skill from what it saw.
Build three skills live with Aton's team's templates and a review rubric.

sections.label: Pick the job
sections.h2: Start with a job you do well and often.
body: p

A skill for a job you are bad at teaches the AI to be bad at it. Pick something you do well, do often, and could explain to a new hire in ten minutes. Writing the follow-up text after a customer conversation. Screening an applicant. Turning a meeting into three action items.
checks
You do it at least weekly.
You could explain it to someone new in ten minutes.
You can name what a bad version looks like.

sections.label: The template
body: code

# [Skill name]

Purpose: [one sentence: the job, and when to use this]
Inputs: [what I give you. If missing, ask before starting]
Steps:
1. ...
2. ...
3. ...
Rules:
- Never ...
- Always ...
Format: [what the output looks like, word limit]
Example: [one real output, done right]
p

Write the steps the way you would say them out loud to a new hire, in order. Write the rules from your mistakes: every rule is something that went wrong once. Put one real example at the bottom. The example teaches more than the steps.

sections.label: Test it
sections.h2: Run it three times before you trust it.
body: steps
An easy case.
Clean inputs, obvious answer. It should be right the first time.
A messy case.
Missing information, a contradiction, an edge. The skill should ask, not guess.
A case where the right answer is no.
Where the job should not be done at all. The skill should say so.
p
If it fails a test, fix the skill file, not the prompt. Then run all three again.

sections.label: Three mistakes
body: steps
Too long.
A skill over a page gets skimmed by the AI the same way a long handbook gets skimmed by a person. Cut it.
No rules.
Steps without rules produce confident, wrong output. The rules are where your judgment lives.
No example.
One real example of the job done right is worth ten sentences describing it.
said
What the coach says
Your skill has fourteen steps and no rules. Cut it to six steps, add the three things that have gone wrong before, and paste in one good example.

ws: Write it the way you would say it to a new hire.
fields: What you always provide. What to ask for if missing.
From your mistakes. Never and always.
What good looks like, and one real one.
pr: Let the AI write it from watching you.
Do the job once in the chat, out loud, then run this.
prompt: I just did a job in this conversation the way I always do it. Write a skill file from what you observed. 1. Purpose in one sentence. 2. Inputs: what I provided, and what you should ask for if it is missing next time. 3. Steps: the order I actually worked in, numbered, no adjectives. 4. Rules: anything I corrected, avoided, or refused to do. Write each as never or always. 5. Format: what my final output looked like, with a word limit. 6. Example: the output from this conversation, cleaned of any private details. Keep the whole file under 250 words. Mark anything you inferred rather than saw with [confirm].
